newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland generators may face MMC review - report.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland generators may face MMC review - report.

text.p: Northern Ireland's electricity regulator Ofreg could refer the region's three generating companies to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) because of a dispute over power prices, the Independent said on Friday.

The newspaper said independent research into the industry by the London Economics consultancy group was sent to Ofreg head Douglas McIldoon on Monday, looking at suggestions put forward by the generators aimed at avoiding a referral to the MMC.

The Independent quoted Charles Coulthard, deputy regulator at Ofreg, as saying the report would give "a clear indication in policy terms. Douglas (McIldoon) will then have to decide whether to refer the generators to the MMC".
The newspaper said offers of power price cuts were "not thought sufficient to satisfy Ofreg".
Ofreg caused a stir earlier this month when it decided on steeper price cuts for Northern Ireland Electricity, the regional supplier, than the MMC had recommended.
Northern Ireland Electricity had called for an MMC review last year after a bitter clash with Ofreg over price controls.
